To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the choice of the convolutional neural network is crucial and (2) the choice of pretext task is not as critical as the choice of CNN.

(1) the choice of the convolutional neural network architecture is crucial for self-supervised visual learning, (2) the number of layers in a network is more important than its width, and (3) a large number of layers is required for self-supervised representation to be competitive with supervised learning.

(i) the choice of CNN architecture is critical for self-supervised representation; (ii) the number of parameters is not a reliable indicator of performance; (iii) a small number of convolutional layers is sufficient; and (iv) self-supervised models can be successfully fine-tuned with very few labeled examples.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (i) How to choose the architecture for CNNs?
the following questions: (1) How to design a good CNN for self-supervised representation?
the following questions: (1) What is the impact of the CNN design on the performance of self-supervised representation?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
self-supervised representation should not be trained on a single pretext task, and that the choice of CNN matters.
, while the performance of self-supervised learning is highly correlated with the choice of the pretext task, the choice of CNN architecture is not a trivial matter.
the best self-supervised visual representations are learned using a simple convolutional neural network, a simple contrastive loss and a simple data augmentation scheme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
self-supervised visual learning has not reached its full potential.
the performance of self-supervised visual representations is highly sensitive to the choice of the pretext task, CNN, data, and training details.
we challenge common practices and propose a number of new techniques to boost the performance of self-supervised representation models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
self-supervised visual learning is a complex problem that requires a careful choice of pretext task and network architecture.
a number of standard design practices for CNNs do not translate to the self-supervised setting.
, while there is still a large room for improvement for self-supervised representation models, the community is now in a better position to develop better methods.
